title: Create Event
description: Creates one event with the specified details.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional header for making the request idempotent

uid.description: The application-specific ID you've given to the user.

id.description: The Fullstory-assigned user ID. This value is returned in a `POST /v2/users` (create user) response.

user.description:
The user identifier.

If `session.id` is provided, the `session.id` is enough to identify a session for which to create the event, and `user` will not be accepted.

If `session.use_most_recent` is set to `true`, one and only one`user` field is required.

id.description: The Fullstory generated identifier for the session to associate the event with. If this session has recorded too much activity, the request is rejected with `code: session_page_limit_exceeded`; see the `session` field description.

use_most_recent.description:
Associate events with the most recent session captured from the user. Defaults to `false`.`

If set to `true`, a `user` is required. The user must have a session within the past 30 minutes, otherwise the events will be created for the user without a session.

It is recommended to use `session.id` instead, when creating events for a specific session.

If the matched session has recorded too much activity, Fullstory starts a new session for the event instead of continuing to add to it; no error is returned in this case.

uid.description: The application-specific ID you've given to the session.

session.description:
The session identifier. If `use_most_recent` is specified to `true` then the most recent session within 30 minutes will be used. If no recent session is found or `use_most_recent` is `false` or not specified, then a session with the provided `id` would be used. If that session is not found or the `id` is not provided, then the events will be created without a session.

Fullstory groups a session's events into a bounded number of internal "pages" as they're recorded. A session that has recorded an unusually large volume of activity can exhaust that internal limit; when that happens, `id`/`uid` targeting is rejected with `code: session_page_limit_exceeded` (send later events to a new session instead), while `use_most_recent` instead starts a new session for you automatically, with no error returned.

browser.description: The browser context in which the events are attached to.

mobile.description: The mobile context in which the events are attached to.

device.description: The device context in which the events are attached to.

location.description: The location context in which the events are attached to.

context.description: The context in which the events are attached to.

timestamp.description: Optional. The event's timestamp represented in ISO 8601 format. If not provided, the current Fullstory server time will be used. It is recommended to always set the timestamp.

schema.description: Optional. Schema declaration, to define the structure of the data, the schema will override Fullstory's default type inference.

properties.description: A mapping of field names to their corresponding types.

page_properties.description: Optional. Page-scoped properties that get denormalized onto all events on the page, enabling search and filtering by page-level metadata.

page_properties_schema.description: Optional. Schema declaration for page_properties, to define the structure of the data. The schema will override Fullstory's default type inference.

properties.description: A mapping of field names to their corresponding types.
